newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Michelin buys Hungary tyremaker Taurus.
newsitem.headline: Michelin buys Hungary tyremaker Taurus.

text.p: Compagnie Financiere Michelin (CFM), the Swiss holding company for France's Michelin, will buy a 90 percent stake in Hungarian agricultural tyremaker Taurus Rt, the national privatisation agency APV Rt announced on Thursday.

Michelin, selected on the basis of its tender offer for Hungary's biggest tyremaker, will pay 1.6 billion forints ($10.4 million) for Taurus, APV's general director Istvan Kocsis told a news conference.

He said Michelin will cover all of Taurus's liabilities to APV, amounting to 8.26 billion forints. Michelin will pay in cash and has agreed to invest an amount equal to the purchase price in the Budapest-based tyremaker, Kocsis added.

Michelin agreed to maintain the brandname Taurus and undertook not to make redundancies of more than 10 percent over the next three years, Kocsis said. The company had 4,147 employees as of last year.
Taurus made 552 million forints in pre-tax profit in 1995 on sales of 18.5 billion forints, 63 percent of which was exports, mostly to Western Europe.

Kocsis said 18 firms had expressed interest in Taurus and three made bids, two of them strong. Other tyremakers known to have been interested in Taurus were Bridgestone Corp, Continental AG and Goodyear Tire & Rubber Co.
